steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Depression symptoms: persistent low mood, loss of interest/pleasure (anhedonia), changes in sleep and appetite, fatigue, difficulty concentrating, feelings of worthlessness, and suicidal thoughts. Diagnosis requires symptoms lasting at least 2 weeks.

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Biological explanations: genetics (twin studies show 37% concordance in MZ vs 15% in DZ twins - McGuffin et al.); neurotransmitter imbalance (low serotonin and noradrenaline); the diathesis-stress model: genetic predisposition + life events trigger depression.

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Cognitive explanations: Beck's negative triad - negative views about the self, the world, and the future create a cycle of depression. Seligman's learned helplessness: repeated failure leads to belief that outcomes are uncontrollable, causing depression.

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Biological treatment: SSRIs (e.g. Prozac) increase serotonin by preventing reuptake at synapses. Effective for many but: side effects (nausea, insomnia, loss of libido), 30-40% of patients don't respond, treats symptoms not causes, withdrawal effects.

steps.title: Try it yourself
steps.body: Describe biological and cognitive explanations of depression and evaluate each one. | Compare SSRI medication with CBT as treatments for depression. | Evaluate whether depression is best explained as a biological or a psychological condition.

steps.title: Exam tips
steps.body: Beck's negative triad: Negative SELF + Negative WORLD + Negative FUTURE = depression. SSRIs = increase serotonin (biological). CBT = change negative thoughts (cognitive). Best = BOTH combined. Diathesis-stress model: GENETIC vulnerability + LIFE EVENTS = depression. Nature + nurture.
